items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: This guy came up there and played so much more piano than I do — it was embarrassing. His name was Mike LeDonne.

ctx.x: The way that you’ve learned, you’ve played with a lot of great musicians, is jazz education different now? And is it better or is it missing something?

Well see you’re asking the wrong guy. I don’t know anything about jazz education. I don’t even understand how there could be such a term as jazz education. But I know it’s going on. In fact the very university, Indiana University where I went to school, and I © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

said they frowned on jazz. Well now it’s known as one of the best schools I guess in the country to teach jazz. And so I mean never having, no one’s ever asked me to you know, lecture or say anything in front of young students, so I just wouldn’t know much about that. I guess there are ways of teaching it but I don’t know how it’s done really. Ignorant about that. You know one pianist, by the way, when he was about eighteen years old, kept hanging around me trying to get me to teach, you know give him lessons.…
